bib.title: RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Generation

question: How can a code language model use the rest of a repository to complete unfinished code, when the unfinished code alone is a poor retrieval query?
hypothesis: Using the model's own generated completion to build the next retrieval query bridges the gap between the retrieval context and the completion target, beating single-pass retrieval-augmented generation.
contributions: RepoCoder: an iterative retrieval-generation framework for repository-level code completion
RepoEval: a benchmark with line, API invocation and function body completion, with unit-test evaluation
Experiments showing RepoCoder beats In-File completion and vanilla RAG

method.summary: A frozen retriever (Jaccard over tokens in a sliding window of repo code) fetches snippets using the last lines of the unfinished code; a frozen code LM completes. In iterations after the first, the query is the last (Sw-Ss) lines of the unfinished code plus the first Ss lines of the previous prediction. No training; evaluated on the new RepoEval benchmark.
method.task: repository-level code completion (line, API invocation, function body)

datasets.name: RepoEval line completion
datasets.split: 200 random lines from each of 8 repos
datasets.source: GitHub Python repos created after 2022-01-01, >100 stars, >80% Python, non-fork, explicit unit tests, open-source licence; archived Jan 2023
datasets.preprocessing: lines non-repetitive, not comments, at least 5 tokens

datasets.name: RepoEval API invocation completion
datasets.split: 200 non-repetitive in-repository API invocations from each of the same 8 repos
datasets.preprocessing: invocations located by parsing the repos

datasets.name: RepoEval function body completion
datasets.preprocessing: functions covered by unit tests, bodies of 3 to 30 lines

models.name: GPT-3.5-Turbo
models.params: inferred: not stated beyond 'billions of trainable parameters'

models.name: UniXcoder
models.architecture: dense code embedding, cosine similarity (Appendix B only)

inference.max_tokens: prompt plus output 4096 (GPT-3.5-Turbo) / 2048 (CodeGen); generated completion max 100 (line, API), 500 (function body)
inference.prompting: Retrieved snippets in ascending order of similarity, each with its original file path, followed by the unfinished code (Fig 3); zero-shot
inference.retrieval: Jaccard over token sets; sliding window of Sw lines moved by Ss lines over repo files; K=10 max snippets; retrieved context set to half the prompt length; iteration 1 query = last Sw lines of X; iteration i>1 query = last (Sw-Ss) lines of X + first Ss lines of previous prediction

other.seeds: not stated; single run per cell implied but not stated
other.stopping: no stopping criterion; Limitations say none found

metrics.name: Exact Match (EM)
metrics.definition: 1 if prediction equals ground truth, else 0, averaged

metrics.name: Pass Rate (PR)
metrics.definition: 1 if completed function passes all repository unit tests, else 0

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.definition: share of retrieved sets containing an invocation example of the ground-truth API

baselines: Oracle (retrieval using the last Sw-Ss lines of X plus first Ss lines of ground truth)
eval.protocol: Single reported value per cell; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. Hyper-parameters set 'based on our experience' and said to be not very sensitive; no sweep shown.

evidence.quote: the maximum number of tokens in the generated completion ( Ŷ ), the line length of the sliding window (Sw), and the sliding size (Ss) are set to 100, 20, and 10 respectively.

results.claim: Iterations are not monotone: from iter 3 to 4 on API completion, GPT-3.5-Turbo gains 10 and loses 14 correct completions (790 vs 794 correct).

limits: Little gain when a repo has few duplicated code lines (Appendix C, Fig 4); correlation with duplication is not absolute.
No way to pick the number of iterations; later iterations can fail cases earlier ones passed (Table 8); no stopping criterion found.
Extra retrieval-generation rounds add latency; not measured.
Prompt template, retrieval models beyond Jaccard and UniXcoder, and stronger code models (GPT-4, StarCoder, WizardCoder) not explored.
Baselines are only In-File and Oracle; commercial tools (Copilot, Tabnine, CodeWhisperer) only in one qualitative case (Appendix E).
EM undercounts correct completions; many EM failures are functionally correct (Appendix D).
Python only; repos from 2022 chosen to avoid training leakage for 2021-cutoff models; single run, no variance reported.
